body:
Tested locally, it works as expected. Code looks good to me.

I've tried to benchmark before/after compilation times on a clean build with all caches removed, but got basically the same results:

```bash
# vstask template = scons -j32 scu_build=all linker=mold platform=linuxbsd target=template_release optimize=speed disable_path_overrides=no
# vstask clean = scons -j32 -c scu_build=all linker=mold platform=linuxbsd target=template_release optimize=speed disable_path_overrides=no

$ hyperfine -iw1 "ccache -C && vstask clean && vstask template" && gh pr checkout 115732 && git rebase master --no-gpg-sign && hyperfine -iw1 "ccache -C && vstask clean && vstask template"

Benchmark 1: ccache -C && vstask clean && vstask template
  Time (mean ± σ):     108.804 s ±  0.143 s    [User: 2417.601 s, System: 121.390 s]
  Range (min … max):   108.661 s … 109.100 s    10 runs
```

Nonetheless, it's not causing a regression in build times at least. Maybe someone else can try to benchmark it on their end.
